content:
I put together a roadmap (blueprint + matching Lean statements, mostly unproved for now) that tries to get from bare Lie algebra representations all the way to the hydrogen atom's spectrum, using nothing but representation theory, classification of irreducible modules, Casimir elements, that kind of thing.

It's really two projects glued together: a purely algebraic one that has nothing to do with physics, and a physics-flavored one.

Repo's here: https://github.com/TomOleDiem/QuantumRepresentationTheory, and the blueprint's here: https://tomolediem.github.io/QuantumRepresentationTheory/blueprint/

Would love a second opinion from anyone who knows this corner of Mathlib better than I do, especially on whether some of the pieces I think are missing actually already exist somewhere and on the definitions themselves, which I'd rather have picked apart now than later. The point is to give people something concrete to walk toward but still general enough for mathlib aswell.

Some of supersymmetric quantum mechanics in physlib (the 1 contribution did there before got distracted with things that did not fit there). Could attach it there too for the relation of different angular momentum sectors

I really like your idea, but strangely enough, it seems that the core part of it assumes the existence of a finite-dimensional bound-state eigenspace and the corresponding operators, rather than deriving them from the Physlib Hamiltonian?

Yes you are correct. My understanding is that the functional calculus for unbounded self-adjoint operators is still under development. In particular, defining objects like 1/r abstractly as a function of the position operator is not yet available, which is why the current Physlib development works with a regularized Hamiltonian. My blueprint therefore focuses on the algebraic side, assuming the representation and classifying it, rather than the analytic construction. Connecting the two will of course be the end goal.
